subject: How to manage cond. formatting & checkboxes with the new package DT?

messages.author: 2ef256a129b97763
messages.subject: How to manage cond. formatting & checkboxes with the new package DT?
parts:
First of all congrats for htmlwidgets and the new packages coming out: really cool stuff.

I've noticed that  in the current beta of shiny the implementation of Data Tables  does not render anymore the checkboxes built with a callback, e.g. the following does not work:
addCheckbox <- paste0('<input type="checkbox" name="row', 
    dt_[,id], '" value="', dt_[,id], '">',"")

and I suppose nether does the following (as a callback in a specific data table definition)

, callback = "function(table) {
    table.on('change.dt', 'tr td input:checkbox', function() {
      setTimeout(function () {
         Shiny.onInputChange('rows4', 
          $(this).add('tr td input:checkbox:checked').parent().siblings(':last-child').map(function() {
                 return $(this).text();
              }).get())
         }, 10); 
    });
}"

I haven't tried to see if conditional formatting (hacked with another callback) still works, but probably not...

The real issue for me to be able to adopt the new package DT would be:

1. How do I add a checkbox column?
2. How do I do conditional formatting, e.g. RED or GREEN depending on certain ranges of values in a particular cell / column?

Would you be so kind to produce an example for both?

Thanks again for the great work!

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: How to manage cond. formatting & checkboxes with the new package DT?
parts:
1. Perhaps you need the argument escape = FALSE or similar; please see
the help page of ?DT::datatable, and it will be clearer if you can
post a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example that shows
what you expect, otherwise it is a little bit hard to read your mind.

2. Please see the section 2.5.5 (or 2.5.2) of the DT documentation:
http://rstudio.github.io/DT/ It did not give you exactly the example
of coloring, but it should be straightforward to adapt it if you are
familiar with JavaScript/jQuery.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: How to manage cond. formatting & checkboxes with the new package DT?
parts:
Please find a simplified code attached. 
  1. Rather than use a checkboxGroupInput element it would look better to have the picker in the actual data table, but I'm not sure how to do this.
  2. Next step would be use conditional formatting on the table: e.g. any entry changed by the sliders below
    a threshold could be amber or red,      but also in this case I'm not sure how to do this.
library(shiny)
library(data.table)

#
dt_ = data.table( Month = month.abb[1:5],
A=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
B=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
C=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
D=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
E=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4))

dt_[,id :=.I]
dt <- copy(dt_)
setkey(dt_, "Month") 
setkey(dt, "Month")

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
fluidRow(
  column(4, 
    actionButton("saveButton", "Update Model"))),
fluidRow(
  column(6, dataTableOutput('DT')),
  column(3, br(),br(),checkboxGroupInput("pick",h6("Picker"), 
    month.abb[1:5])),  
  column(3, uiOutput('foo'))),
fluidRow(
  column(4, verbatimTextOutput('vals')))    
  ),

  server = function(session,input, output) {
    valPpu <- reactiveValues()

    valPpu$buttonF <- 1
##
  output$DT <- renderDataTable({
  if(length(input$pick) > 0 ) {

    labs <- isolate( input$pick )
    buttn <- isolate( valPpu$buttonF )
    iter <- length(labs)   
    valLabs <- sapply(1:iter, function(i) {
            as.numeric(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]]) })

    if( iter == sum(sapply(valLabs,length)) ) {        

          cPerc <- valLabs
          cPerc <- as.data.table(cPerc)
          cPercDt <- cbind(Month=labs,cPerc)
          
          ival <- which(dt[["Month"]] 
              %in% cPercDt[["Month"]])
          setkey(cPercDt, "Month") 
          for(j in LETTERS[1:5]) set(dt_, i=ival, 
          j=j, dt[cPercDt][[j]] * (1 + dt_[cPercDt][["cPerc"]]) )

  } }

  dt_[order(id),]
  }, options = list(
  scrollX = TRUE,
  scrollY = "250px" ,
  scrollCollapse = TRUE,
  paging = FALSE,
  searching = FALSE,
  ordering = FALSE )
)
##
  output$foo <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
    if(length(input$pick) > 0 ) {
      iter <- length(input$pick)
      buttn <- isolate( valPpu$buttonF )
      valLabs <- sapply(1:iter, function(i) {
      if(is.null(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]] )) {
                0
      } else {  as.numeric(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]])  }
      }) 
  #
  toRender <- lapply(1:iter, function(i) {
    sliderInput(inputId = paste0(month.abb[i], "_v",buttn),
                label =  h6(paste0(month.abb[i],"")),
                min = -1,
                max = 1,
                step = 0.01,
                value = valLabs[i],
                format = "##0.#%",
                locale = "gb", ticks = FALSE, animate = FALSE)
                })
     
      toRender
    }
    })


    observe({

  if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
  if(input$saveButton < valPpu$buttonF) { return() }
  valPpu$buttonF <- valPpu$buttonF + 1
# TODO: saving code  
})
  }
)
